key_insight: A dual-scale deep learning framework that combines 10x and 20x histopathology, plus clinical metadata, can help distinguish mycosis fungoides from non-MF skin conditions.
clinical_relevance: The approach is aimed at earlier screening support for MF and a separate clinical model for staging confirmed cases, which could improve dermatology diagnostic workflows.
method: Late-fusion ensemble of CNNs using dual-magnification slides (10x and 20x)
Random forest classifier trained on 16 clinical features
Two-task design: MF vs non-MF screening and patch/plaque vs tumor staging
evidence_signal: On an expanded dataset of 6,267 images from 463 patients, the image model reached 83.58% accuracy and 89.13% sensitivity, while the clinical model reached 96.6% accuracy and 93.8% sensitivity.
watch_item: Performance may depend on dataset quality and external validation, and the image-based model is not a standalone diagnostic substitute for expert pathology review.
paper_title: Detail in Context: A Dual-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Mycosis Fungoides Detection
